newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds higher across the board.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds higher across the board.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were higher across the board and yield spreads to comparable Treasuries narrowed by a couple of ticks late in the session Tuesday, traders said.
Premium coupon pass-throughs seemed to be the flavor of a relatively light trading day, said one Ginnie trader.
"There wasn't a whole lot of activity, but there was good buying in 7.5 percent and 8.0 percent coupons," he said.
Prices of Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 6/32 at 100-22/32 bid, yielding 97 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were up 4/32 at 100-16/32 bid, and Freddie Mac paper rose 5/32 at 100-22/32 bid.
"I don't know why people are so interested in 8.0 percent coupons, given the high dollar price," said another pass-through trader.
He said that pass-through prices failed to trade up as much as investors had expected over the last couple of days, and that may be one reason why some market players sought premium coupons.
"Theoretically, they shouldn't, given the dollar price and the position in interest rates," he said.
The Treasury sold $15.5 billion in two-year notes at 6.027 percent in an auction that, on balance, was relatively well received.
In Treasury trading, the five-year Treasury note was up 2/32 to yield 6.30 percent, and the 10-year Treasury note was up 3/32, yielding 6.41 percent.
